% Input by Péter-Dániel Szántó % Michaelmas 2008, Oxford % Unnumbered folios, clearly out of sequence
The text identifies its dhāraṇī as that of Vasudhārā (cf.
Padmanabh S. Jaini’s edition of this text, which is also used by Jains);
however, this text appears to be a different recension of the dhāraṇī.

And it does not correspond exactly with the Vajradhara in Tōh. 662 (1007? CHECK). [1] Oṃ, homage to all nāgas, svāhā! Oṃ, homage to all yakṣas, svāhā! Oṃ, homage to all grahas, svāhā! Oṃ, homage to the lord of all rākṣasas, svāhā! Oṃ, homage to the lord of all bhūtas...
[2] Homage, svāhā! Oṃ, homage to the Lord of all pretas, svāhā! Oṃ, homage to all piśācas, svāhā! Oṃ, homage to all pravaṇas, svāhā! Oṃ, homage to all maruts, svāhā!
[3] Oṃ, homage to all great maruts, svāhā! Oṃ, homage to all Mahākālas, svāhā! Oṃ, homage to all Mothers, svāhā! Oṃ, homage to all Bhṛṅgārīs, svāhā!

[4] Oṃ, homage to all *bhūtanīs*, svāhā! Oṃ, homage to all *piśācinīs*, svāhā! Oṃ, homage to all *yakṣiṇīs*, svāhā! For these, for me, for [Name], and for all sentient beings, bestow all wealth, grain, gold, and treasures; cause them to be given to me, svāhā! Oṃ, to the illustrious Jambhala, Lord of Waters, bring all substances; cause them to be given to me, svāhā! Oṃ svāhā! Bhū svāhā! \exposure 3\upper
[1] *Bhuvaḥ svāhā*! *Svaḥ svāhā*! *Oṃ bhūr bhuvaḥ svaḥ svāhā*! *Oṃ daśabhyo digbhyaḥ svāhā*! May they grant me my desire; may they rejoice without delay. These are the mantra words:
[2] *Oṃ oṃ oṃ oṃ oṃ* | *Hūṃ hūṃ hūṃ hūṃ hūṃ* | *Hrīṃ hrīṃ hrīṃ hrīṃ hrīṃ* | *Kṣemārogya dhanaṃ dehi dadāpaya svāhā*! This heart-mantra accomplishes all rites. [It is] the size of a man—

[3] ...he bestows great wealth. He fulfills one’s desired wishes. For, O son of good family, those who maintain this dhāraṇī named Vasudhārā—by the power of this dhāraṇī, all diseases, famines, and pestilences do not prevail. Furthermore, O son of good family, whoever, having performed worship to the Tathāgatas, Arhats, and Samyaksambuddhas, [recites] these mantra-words of the Vasudhārā-nāma-dhāraṇī for six months...

[5] I shall turn back those [obstacles]; then, in whatever place one is engaged—whether for the purpose of prosperity in one’s own house or another’s house—the Tathāgata, the Noble Avalokiteśvara, [will grant success]. All...

He said this to him: "I would like to ask the Blessed One, the Tathāgata, the Arhat, the Samyaksambuddha, about a certain matter, if the Blessed One would grant me the opportunity to have my question answered. When this had been said, the Blessed One spoke thus to the householder Sucandra: "Ask, householder, whatever you desire; I shall satisfy your mind by answering your questions accordingly."

[3] — ...ṣye. When this had been said, the householder Sucandra, having replied to the Blessed One, "Very well, Blessed One," addressed the Blessed One as follows: "Blessed One, how does a son of good family or a daughter of good family, having been poor, become no longer poor; and how, being ill, becomes no longer ill? Then the Blessed One, knowing full well, spoke thus to the householder Sucandra: [Exposure 4] upper section.

[1] “Householder, why do you ask about poverty? When this was said, the householder Sucandra addressed the Blessed One as follows: “I am poor, Blessed One; I am poor, Sugata. I have many sons, many daughters, and am endowed with many servants and attendants. Therefore, may the Blessed One teach me a Dharma-discourse by which impoverished beings might become non-indigent, and those who are sick might become healthy.”

[3] They shall possess abundant wealth, and their granaries, treasuries, and storehouses shall be full. They shall be dear, pleasant, and delightful to behold. As lords of generosity, they shall have inexhaustible silver, gold, wealth, grain, jewels, treasuries, and storehouses;

they shall be enriched with all manner of goods—gems, pearls, diamonds, lapis lazuli, conch shells, crystals, coral, gold, silver, emeralds, rubies, sapphires, karketana stones, and so forth. They shall be well-established, possessing houses, sons, wives, and households.
[Break] Exposure 4, lower [1]:

By means of a spy, Sucandra’s minister approached, entered the interior, and saw that it was filled with an abundance of all kinds of wealth, grain, and jewels; he saw that the great treasuries and granaries were full.

[2] Delighted, thrilled, satisfied, elated, joyful, and filled with gladness and cheer, he approached the Blessed One. Then the venerable Ānanda, struck with wonder and filled with gladness and cheer, said this to the Blessed One: "Blessed One, what is the cause, what is the condition, by which the householder Sucandra has become so immensely wealthy, possessing great treasuries and storehouses overflowing with grain?"
The Blessed One said: “O noble son, the householder Sucandra is most excellent; he is a supreme, virtuous refuge.

He has upheld this dhāraṇī named Vasudhārā, and he will take it up, uphold it, recite it, master it, rejoice in it, and reveal it in detail to others. Therefore, Ānanda, you too should take up the Vasudhārā.”

[2] + "O Āma, uphold this *dhāraṇī*; grasp it, recite it, teach it, master it, and reveal it in detail to others. It will be for the benefit of many, for the happiness of many, out of compassion for the world, and for the welfare, benefit, and happiness of the great multitude of beings, both gods and humans, for whomsoever, O householder, it shall come into their hands or be found in written books. For that person, du-"

[4] There is no fear for one who begs; gradually, his wealth increases. Ānanda, I do not perceive anyone in the world with its gods, Māras, and Brahmās, among this generation of recluses and brahmins—[break]—who [could prevent this].

They do not cause harm; those who feed on fat do not cause harm; those who feed on marrow do not cause harm; those who feed on phlegm do not cause harm; those who feed on excrement do not cause harm; those who feed on breath do not cause harm;

those who feed on fragrance do not cause harm; those who feed on incense do not cause harm; those who feed on flowers do not cause harm; those who feed on fruit do not cause harm; those who feed on grain—

The *rā* do not cause harm; the *garbhāhāra* do not cause harm. For the purpose of striking, bursting, splitting, and smiting the heads of all these wicked ones with the great vajra: *HŪṂ HŪṂ PHAṬ*. With the vajra, slay, slay! Dry up, dry up! Paralyze, paralyze! Bind, bind! Kill, kill! Burn, burn! Crush, crush! Destroy, destroy! All enemies! *HŪṂ HŪṂ PHAṬ SVĀHĀ*. And for whomsoever, O noble son...

[5] Or for a son of good family or a daughter of good family— whether it has entered their heart, entered their home, come into their hands, been committed to a book, or merely heard; whether it has been mastered, retained, recited, reflected upon, approved, or extensively proclaimed to others— for that son of good family or daughter of good family, it will lead to long-lasting welfare, benefit, happiness, security, and prosperity.

[2] ...will come to pass. Whoever, having performed worship and paid homage to the Tathāgatas, should recite this dhāraṇī named *Vasudhārā* three or four times at midnight, the deities—becoming joyful, delighted, glad, and full of mental well-being—will themselves come and cause a rain of grain to fall. Out of affection for the teaching of the Tathāgata; out of affection for the designation of the Buddha; out of affection for the designation of the Dharma.

[4] With joy, through the designation of the Saṅgha; with joy, through the intention of the Dharma-preacher: *Oṃ, homage to the Blessed One, the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha Vajradharasāgaranirghoṣa*.
Homage to all Tathāgatas of the past, future, and present. Homage to the Tathāgata Kṣemaṅkara. Homage to the Tathāgata Vajragarbha.
O Blessed One, may the desires of the practitioners be fulfilled; arise, O Vidyās, all Buddhas, Blessed Ones, give your command! Svāhā!
[2] Homage to all the Tathāgatas of the three times. It is as follows: Oṃ śrī surūpe svāhā! Oṃ śrī divyarūpe svāhā! Oṃ śrī dīptarūpe svāhā! Oṃ śrī vasurūpe svāhā!

[3] Oṃ śrī jñānarūpe svāhā | Oṃ śrī prajñāpāramite svāhā | Oṃ śrī vajrasattvahṛdaye svāhā | Oṃ śrī bhadre svāhā | Oṃ śrī subhadre svāhā | Oṃ śrī bhadramati svāhā | Oṃ śrī subhadramati svāhā | Oṃ śrī maṅgale svāhā | Oṃ śrī maṅgalamati svāhā | Oṃ śrī ālaye svāhā | Oṃ śrī ale 2 svāhā | Oṃ cale 2 svāhā |

[Exposure 8, lower margin 1] ((Pu))ja said: "If anyone should act otherwise toward this *vidyā*, or should transgress it, such a thing is impossible. Why is that? Because, Ānanda, these mantra-words called the *dhāraṇī* 'Inexhaustible Stream of Wealth' (*Anandavasudhārā*) are indeed indestructible;
they do not even come to the ears of those beings whose roots of merit are exhausted. How much more so for one who shall hold them in a book or within their heart, and shall recite them?"

[3] For what reason? This speech of all the Tathāgatas has been spoken, empowered, sealed with their own seals, revealed, rejoiced in, illuminated, praised, extolled, explained, made clear, and approved by these Tathāgatas. At that moment, the venerable Ānanda said to the Blessed One, “Excellent, excellent, Blessed One! and spoke this verse: [4] ...
(exposure 9) ... (Note: The bracketed portions indicate textual fragments or lacunae in the source manuscript.)
[1] O you who are always abundant with material wealth, with gold enriched by many jewels; you who fill my homes with this mandala—homage to you, Śrī Vasudhārā, forever!

[2] The Blessed One is the Buddha; the qualities of a Buddha are also inconceivable. For those who have approached the destruction [of defilements], the ripening [of their merit] is likewise inconceivable. You are the Teacher, the noble one, the All-Knowing One, the lineage of the Dharma-Kings. O Heroic Buddha, who has gone to the further shore and attained the fruit—homage be to you! Then, indeed, the Venerable Ānanda, joyful, satisfied, elated, uplifted in mind, and filled with gladness, joy, and happiness, addressed the Blessed One...

[4] He addressed him who possessed such qualities as follows: "How, Blessed One, shall I uphold this Dharma-discourse? The Blessed One said: "Uphold it also as 'The Inquiry of the Householder Sucandra. [Sarvadhana...]"

[1] May Dhanada, Varuṇa, Indra, and likewise Vaivasvata, following the mind’s intent, constantly contemplate and bestow everything! May there be the accomplishment of whatever is desired; of this there is no doubt. Khaṭa 2 khiṭi 2 khuṭu 2 [2] muru 2 muruṇḍa 2 tarppari 2 dehi dadāpaya svāhā! Arise, O Hiraṇyasuvarṇadhārā, svāhā! For clothing and ornaments, svāhā! For vehicles, svāhā! O Vasudhā, svāhā!

[3] Svāhā to the Lord of the Earth! Svāhā to Gau! Svāhā to Surata! Svāhā to Indra! Svāhā to the Pañcikas! Svāhā to Yama! Svāhā to Varuṇa! Svāhā to Vaiśravaṇa! [4] Oṃ, bestow upon me treasures of beings, wealth, and grain; cause them to be given! Svāhā! Oṃ, to Vasudhā, svāhā! Oṃ, to the Lord of the Earth, svāhā! Oṃ, obeisance to all the gods, svāhā!

Exposure 10, Upper [1]: We invoke for wealth and grain; we meditate upon all jewels, garments, ornaments, and all requisites; therefore, may the glorious Vasudhārā impel us—*svāhā*. *Oṃ svāhā*. *Svaḥ svāhā*. *Śrī svāhā*. *Hrī svāhā*. *Svā svāhā*. *Hā svāhā*. *Oṃ*, we invoke the vessel of vehicles; we meditate upon her who goes afar—therefore, *svāhā* to the glorious Vasudhārā. She is the producer of unarisen goods.

And for the increase of substances already produced: *ṭili 2 ṭeli 2 ita 2 āgaccha 2 bhagavati! Fulfill the desires of [name] from the ten directions! Just as the bearer of water fills the earth; just as the rays of the sun dispel darkness; just as the cool-rayed moon causes nourishment; just as the essence of great medicinal herbs destroys all diseases.*

Exposure 10: [1] O you who cause the increase of all jewels, gold, garments, ornaments, and accessories, wealth, and grain; you who arise upon being thought of; you who cause infatuation; you who milk the treasury and granary of Śukra; you who are the opinion of Bṛhaspati; you who take away [the enemy's] mind! [2] By means of the Buddha’s truth! By the truth of the Dharma! By the truth of the Saṅgha! By the truth of all Bodhisattvas! By the truth of those intent on awakening! By the truth of all Śrāvakas and Pratyekabuddhas! By the truth of Brahmā! By the truth of Viṣṇu!

[3] By the truth of Rudra, by the truth of the World-Protectors, O you who carry out the commands of Dhanada! For the abundance of all things—gold, silver, jewels, pearls, diamonds, lapis lazuli, conch shells, crystals, coral, native gold, wrought silver, emeralds, rubies, sapphires, and karketana stones—may sixty thousand measures of rice be brought under one's dominion. Come, O Blessed One, Daughter of the Buddha, as deep as the ocean, wielder of the vajra!

[5] O you who speak the truth! [2] Through the splendor of the Blessed One Vipaśyin, through the power of Śikhin, through the wisdom of Viśvabhū, through the strength of Krakucchanda, through the training of Kanakamuni, through the virtues of Kāśyapa, through the vigor of Śākyasiṃha, and through the vow of Maitreya—may these Tathāgatas be fulfilled! These mantra-words are for the benefit of all beings; they are a vidyā-mantra for the removal of poverty, suffering, and calamity.

[4] To those who liberate from the ocean of debt! I shall proclaim this secret *vidyā* and *dhāraṇī* named *Vasudhārā*. I recollect the mantra-words which are the meaning of what was spoken by the Blessed One. Namely: Oṃ kṣaṃ hūṃ. [5] <x o x> Oṃ Śrī! Dhane dhane! Dhaneśvarye! Srutrumāne! Akṣayakoṣe! Cintitopādani! Manasi sādhanī! Koṭe koṭe! Koṭāvare! Koṭīśvarye! Anantāya yantrabhyaḥ!
